content.title: Fourth Kenya University exhibition
content.summary: The fourth Kenya University exhibition was held at the Kenyatta International Conference Centre from 15 to 18 March 2006.

content.text: The fourth Kenya University exhibition was held at the Kenyatta International Conference Centre from 15 to 18 March 2006. The four-day exhibition was opened on Wednesday by Assistant Minister Education, Mrs. Beth Mugo. It brought together 15 public and private universities, one constituent college, the Commission of Higher Education (CHE), the Joint Admissions Board (JAB) and the Higher Education Loans Board (HELB). It was the first time that the JAB was participating at such an event. The institutions advised parents and students on their academic programmes. Vice-chancellors and other heads also held seminars at the same venue on various issues affecting the institutions. The turnout this year was high, and the queries from the public more specific about the programmes being offered by the universities. There was a lot of interest expressed in AKU's programmes, particularly the nursing programmes. The general opinion was that AKU had reached the stage to venture into undergraduate programmes in nursing and medicine, providing alternative to the only two public universities currently offering those programmes. The universities are University of Nairobi and Moi University. There was also interest particularly with AKU Karachi's undergraduate programme in medicine, with the issue of tuition fee and living expenses raised. Application forms and admission related information were given to prospective students, who are finalizing their high school studies this year.
